opt: (A) incomplete — (B) gamble — (C) customs
(A) thorough — (B) safeguard — (C) fads
(A) incomplete — (B) safeguard — (C) customs
(A) incomplete — (B) gamble — (C) fads
(A) thorough — (B) gamble — (C) customs
choice.ex: (A) incomplete (B) gamble (C) customs 근거 ❷❹❺ 해설: (A) ❹ stil young, so much we do not know = 불완전한 / (B) ❷ conducting huge experiments = 위험한 도박 / (C) ❺ eaten certain foods in certain ways for mil ennia = 오래된 음식 관습. thorough(철저한)는 ❹와 반대, safeguard(안전장치)는 ‘위험한 실험’과 반대, fads(일시적 유행)는 ‘수천 년’과 정반대. 요약문 해석: 영양에 대한 우리의 지식은 아직 (A) 불완전하므로, 식단을 급격히 바꾸는 것은 위험한 (B) 도박이다. 대신 우리는 오래된 음식 (C) 관습이 타 당한 이유로 존재한다고 가정해야 한다.
choice.psg: ❶ Human beings have evolved to make the most of the resources available to them in ways that are subtle and complicated. ❷ When we change our diets, especially when we do so quickly, we are effectively conducting huge experiments in nutrition. ❸ We ought to have more humility. ❹ Nutritional science is still young and there is so much we do not know. ❺ If we have eaten certain foods in certain ways for millennia, we should assume until it is proven otherwise that there is probably a good reason why. ❻ Traditional foods that don’t fit neatly on the contemporary dietary food plate should generally be chosen over highly processed ones that do. ❼ We should assume that traditionally made fatty blood sausages are preferable to lean, factory-made salamis; that spoonfuls of honey are superior to sprinkles of sweeteners. ❽ Witnessing how poorly traditional societies are faring as they undergo a nutrition transition should make those who have already completed it question whether their diets have moved too far.
choice.body: Because our knowledge of nutrition is still (A)________, rapidly changing our diets is a risky (B)________; we should instead assume that long-standing food (C)________ exist for good reasons.

choice.psg: ❶ Human beings have evolved to make the most of the resources available to them in ways that are subtle and complicated. ❷ When we change our diets, especially when we do so quickly, we are effectively conducting huge experiments in nutrition. ❸ We ought to have more humility. ❹ Nutritional science is still young and there is so much we do not know. ❺ If we have eaten certain foods in certain ways for millennia, we should assume until it is proven otherwise that there is probably a good reason why. ❻ Traditional foods that don’t fit neatly on the contemporary dietary food plate should generally be chosen over highly processed ones that do. ❼ We should assume that traditionally made fatty blood sausages are preferable to lean, factory-made salamis; that spoonfuls of honey are superior to sprinkles of sweeteners. ❽ Witnessing how poorly traditional societies are faring as they undergo a nutrition transition should make those who have already completed it question whether their diets have moved too far.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: Societies that have already changed their diets could learn from those now changing.
Modern dietary guidelines were created mainly to promote the sale of factory-made foods.
Food made in traditional ways can be a wiser choice than food made in factories.
Long-standing eating habits may have benefits that science has not yet explained.
Rapid changes in what we eat carry risks we may not fully understand.
choice.ex: 본문은 현대 식단 기준에 맞지 않는 전통 음식을 우선 선택하라(❻)고 할 뿐, 식단 지침이 공장 음식 판매를 위해 만들어졌다는 동기는 전혀 언급하지 않음(본문 밖 음모론적 추측). 급격한 변화의 위험은 ❷❹, 과학이 설명 못한 이점은 ❹❺, 전통 음식이 더 현명함은 ❻❼, 이미 바꾼 사회가 배움은 ❽에서 추론 가능. ① 근거 ❽ — 이미 식단을 바꾼 사회들은 지금 바뀌고 있는 사회들로부터 배울 수 있다. ② 근거 없음(정답) — 현대 식단 지침은 주로 공장에서 만든 음식의 판매를 촉진하기 위해 만들어졌다. ③ 근거 ❻❼ — 전통 방식으로 만든 음식이 공장에서 만든 음식보다 더 현명한 선택일 수 있다. ④ 근거 ❹❺ — 오래된 식습관에는 과학이 아직 설명하지 못한 이점이 있을 수 있다. ⑤ 근거 ❷❹ — 우리가 먹는 것의 급격한 변화는 우리가 완전히 이해하지 못할 수도 있는 위험을 수반한다.
choice.psg: ❶ Human beings have evolved to make the most of the resources available to them in ways that are subtle and complicated. ❷ When we change our diets, especially when we do so quickly, we are effectively conducting huge experiments in nutrition. ❸ We ought to have more humility. ❹ Nutritional science is still young and there is so much we do not know. ❺ If we have eaten certain foods in certain ways for millennia, we should assume until it is proven otherwise that there is probably a good reason why. ❻ Traditional foods that don’t fit neatly on the contemporary dietary food plate should generally be chosen over highly processed ones that do. ❼ We should assume that traditionally made fatty blood sausages are preferable to lean, factory-made salamis; that spoonfuls of honey are superior to sprinkles of sweeteners. ❽ Witnessing how poorly traditional societies are faring as they undergo a nutrition transition should make those who have already completed it question whether their diets have moved too far.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: discovering safer ways of eating through modern science
returning to the eating habits of our ancestors
measuring the nutrients in the foods we eat every day
carrying out carefully designed scientific studies in laboratories
taking big, uncertain risks with our health without knowing the results
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 우리가 우리의 식단을 바꿀 때, 특히 우리가 매우 빠르게 그렇게 할 때, 우리는 실질적으로 영양 섭취에서 거대한 실험을 시 행하고 있는 것이다. 해설: 식단을 (특히 빠르게) 바꾸는 것을 ‘거대한 영양 실험’에 비유 → 결과를 모르는 채 우리 몸으로 위험을 감수한다는 뜻. 바로 뒤 ❸ 겸손, ❹ 모르는 것 이 많음이 이를 뒷받침. 실험실 연구는 experiment를 글자 그대로 읽은 함정, 더 안전한 방법 발견과 조상 식습관으로 회귀는 정반대, 영양소 측정은 무관. ① 현대 과학을 통해 더 안전한 식사 방법을 발견하는 것 ② 우리 조상들의 식습관으로 돌아가는 것 ③ 우리가 매일 먹는 음식의 영양소를 측정하는 것 ④ 실험실에서 신중하게 설계된 과학 연구를 수행하는 것 ⑤ 결과를 모른 채 우리 건강을 걸고 크고 불확실한 위험을 감수하는 것
choice.body: Human beings have evolved to make the most of the resources available to them in ways that are subtle and complicated. When we change our diets, especially when we do so quickly, we are effectively conducting huge experiments in nutrition. We ought to have more humility.

choice.ex: (A) determine (B) align with (C) open 근거 ❶❷❸❻ 해설: (A) ❶ not the only factors driving ~ decisions = 편리함만으로 결정하지 않음 / (B) ❷ institutions that match their personal beliefs and values = 일치하다 / (C) ❸ Transparency is vital, ❻ clearly communicate fees ~ data = 숨김없는(투명한). clash with(충돌하다)는 match와 반대, secretive(비밀스러운)는 투명성과 반대, hinder(방해하다)는 ‘편리함은 중요하다(crucial)’는 ❶과 어긋남. 요약문 해석: Z세대에게 편리함만으로는 금융 선택을 (A) 결정하지 않는다. 그들은 가치관이 자신의 것과 (B) 일치하고 수수료와 데이터 사용에 대해 완전 히 (C) 숨김없는 은행을 원한다.

choice.body: For Gen Z, convenience alone does not (A)________ financial choices; they want banks whose values (B)________ their own and that are fully (C)________ about fees and data use.

strongly guided by personal principles when choosing where to keep their money
unwilling to trust any bank regardless of its policies
mainly attracted by banks that offer the highest interest rates

choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 이 세대는 매우 가치 지향적이며, 개인의 신념과 가치에 부합하는 기관과 거래하기를 원한다. 해설: ‘가치 지향적’의 의미는 바로 뒤 ‘개인의 신념과 가치에 부합하는 기관과 거래하기를 원한다’가 풀어 줌 → 개인적 원칙(신념)에 따라 은행을 고름. 높 은 이자율과 금전적 가치 극대화는 values를 ‘돈의 가치’로 오해한 함정, 빠른 온라인 서비스는 ❶의 편리함·기술 쪽, 어떤 은행도 믿지 않는다는 것은 ❹(책 무성이 부족한 곳에만 회의적)의 과장. ① 더 빠른 온라인 은행 서비스에 더 많은 돈을 낼 의향이 있는 ② 돈을 어디에 맡길지 선택할 때 개인적 원칙에 강하게 이끌리는 ③ 정책에 관계없이 어떤 은행도 믿으려 하지 않는 ④ 가장 높은 이자율을 제공하는 은행에 주로 끌리는 ⑤ 가능한 한 많은 금전적 가치를 얻는 데 집중하는

choice.ex: (A) slip (B) dehydrated (C) overlooked 근거 ❸❹❺ 해설: (A) ❸ a simple miscalculation = 실수 / (B) ❹ he was analyzing dried spinach = 건조된 / (C) ❺ the correction was just as swiftly forgotten = 간과되다. breakthrough(획기적 발견)는 착오와 반대, raw(날것의)는 dried와 반대, publicized(널리 알려진)는 forgotten과 정반대. 요약문 해석: 시금치에 철분이 풍부하다는 믿음은 계산상의 (A) 실수에서 시작되었다. 한 과학자가 신선한 시금치보다 훨씬 많은 철분을 가진 (B) 건조된 시금치를 검사했고, 그 오류는 수정되었지만 그 수정은 곧 (C) 간과되었다.
choice.psg: ❶ Myths aren’t only stories. ❷ For example, a well-known myth that persists today is the supposed high iron content in spinach. ❸ This is a legend that dates back to 1890 and originates from a simple miscalculation by physiologist Gustav von Bunge. ❹ He accurately determined that 100 grams of spinach contained 35 milligrams of iron but he was analyzing dried spinach, which held ten times more iron than the same amount of fresh leafy greens. ❺ Although the error was swiftly corrected, the correction was just as swiftly forgotten. ❻ The myth had taken hold. ❼ Popeye, who gained superhuman strength from the leafy greens and defended himself with iron fists, contributed to its endurance and even today, some nearly 150 years later, parents the world over use this tale to try to persuade their children into eating the healthy vegetable.
choice.body: The belief that spinach is rich in iron began with a (A)________ in calculation: a scientist tested (B)________ spinach, which holds far more iron than fresh spinach, and although the error was fixed, the fix was soon (C)________.

para.en: Human beings have evolved to make the most of the resources available to them in ways that are subtle and complicated. When we change our diets, especially when we do so quickly, we are effectively conducting huge experiments in nutrition. We ought to have more humility. Nutritional science is still young and there is so much we do not know. If we have eaten certain foods in certain ways for millennia, we should assume until it is proven otherwise that there is probably a good reason why. Traditional foods that don’t fit neatly on the contemporary dietary food plate should generally be chosen over highly processed ones that do. We should assume that traditionally made fatty blood sausages are preferable to lean, factory-made salamis; that spoonfuls of honey are superior to sprinkles of sweeteners. Witnessing how poorly traditional societies are faring as they undergo a nutrition transition should make those who have already completed it question whether their diets have moved too far.

While convenience and technology are crucial, they are not the only factors driving Gen Z’s financial decisions. This generation is incredibly values-driven, and they want to bank with institutions that match their personal beliefs and values. Transparency is vital. Gen Z is skeptical of large corporations and institutions that lack accountability. They have grown up in a world where information is freely available, and they expect complete transparency from the brands they support. Banks, for example, must clearly communicate fees, terms, and conditions, as well as how they handle customers’ data. Moreover, ethical banking practices are more important than ever. Gen Z cares about the environment, social justice, and the ethical implications of their financial decisions. They are interested in sustainable investing, supporting businesses that match their values, and ensuring that their money is not being used to fund harmful practices. Banks that offer socially responsible investment opportunities and are committed to environmental sustainability will attract Gen Z’s attention.

Myths aren’t only stories. For example, a well-known myth that persists today is the supposed high iron content in spinach. This is a legend that dates back to 1890 and originates from a simple miscalculation by physiologist Gustav von Bunge. He accurately determined that 100 grams of spinach contained 35 milligrams of iron but he was analyzing dried spinach, which held ten times more iron than the same amount of fresh leafy greens. Although the error was swiftly corrected, the correction was just as swiftly forgotten. The myth had taken hold. Popeye, who gained superhuman strength from the leafy greens and defended himself with iron fists, contributed to its endurance and even today, some nearly 150 years later, parents the world over use this tale to try to persuade their children into eating the healthy vegetable.

The technical term often used to describe animals’ judgement of numbers is the approximate number system. What it does not provide is precision. It shows ― and this is the same in every species tested ― a characteristic pattern of errors, with discrimination becoming less accurate as the quantities get bigger. Rhesus monkeys can tell one from two, two from three, three from four, four from five ... but start to fail from five upwards. Rats that learned to press a lever a given number of times, from four up to twenty-four, became markedly less and less precise in their responses as the number increased: by the top end of the range they would merely produce a spread of numbers around the target. It is a common observation that when testing the accuracy of animals’ number sense, the size of the numbers matters.

Despite the cultural trope depicting emotions as the opposite of rational thought, cognition ― what we commonly refer to as thinking ― is actually a key building block of emotion. How we think about our circumstances shapes the emotions we experience; then those emotions echo back to influence how we think. For instance, if you walk into a test thinking you are bad at taking tests, your anxiety will be increased. Then you don’t feel good about your performance on the test, and that becomes evidence for continuing to think that you’re bad at test taking. In this way there’s simply no pulling emotion and cognition apart. This bi-directionality of cognition and emotion allows us to adjust difficult emotions by changing the way we think. By thinking differently ― I get nervous sometimes, but I’m still a good test taker, or that nervous feeling is just excitement and anticipation, it means I’m ready ― you can work those pathways to your advantage.

howto.word: 단락마다 밑줄 친 (번호) 중 어법·어휘상 틀린 것을 찾아요. 밑줄이 하나씩 나오면 O(맞음) 또는 X(틀림)를 누르고, X는 바로 아래 칸에 고쳐 씁니다. 어휘는 원문과 단어가 달라도 뜻이 같으면 O, 글의 흐름과 반대면 X예요. 틀린 부분만 써도 되고 밑줄 전체나 문장 전체로 고쳐 써도 됩니다(정답이 들어 있으면 정답). 밑줄을 모두 O·X 해야 다음 단락으로 넘어가요.
howto.word2: 단락마다 밑줄 친 (번호) 중 어법·어휘상 틀린 것을 찾아요. 밑줄이 하나씩 나오면 O(맞음) 또는 X(틀림)를 누르고, X는 바로 아래 칸에 고쳐 씁니다. 심화: 원문과 표현·구조가 달라도 어법상 옳고 뜻이 같으면 O, 어법이 틀리거나 글의 흐름과 반대되면 X예요. 틀린 부분만 써도 되고 밑줄 전체나 문장 전체로 고쳐 써도 됩니다(정답이 들어 있으면 정답). 밑줄을 모두 O·X 해야 다음 단락으로 넘어가요.
howto.cloze: 빈칸을 하나씩 보여 줘요. 우리말 뜻·유의어·첫 글자 힌트를 보고 원문 표현 그대로 쓰고 Enter(또는 다음 빈칸)를 누르세요. 빈칸을 모두 채워야 다음 지문으로 넘어가요.
howto.tf: 글과 일치하면 T, 아니면 F를 누르세요. 문장을 하나씩 보여 주고, 누르면 다음 문장으로 넘어가요. 지문은 아래 상자 안에서 스크롤하며 읽어요. 결과 화면에서 F 문장의 고칠 부분과 근거를 확인하세요.
howto.choice: 요약문 빈칸 · 추론할 수 없는 것 · 밑줄 의미를 고르는 5지선다예요. 지문은 상자 안에서 스크롤해요.
howto.order: 단락 (A)~(D)를 원래 글의 순서대로 눌러 주세요. 원문은 볼 수 없어요.
howto.insert: 주어진 문장이 들어갈 번호를 누르세요. 원문은 볼 수 없어요.
